body:
TRIAGED ALL FIVE AND REVIEWED THE ONE THAT WAS ACTUALLY UNREVIEWED. Headline: the reviewer seat is not tonight's constraint, and I can show it.

THE TRIAGE, checked by comparing each PR's head sha against its recorded verdict's reviewed_sha:

    #1972  head 6512f1312a  CHANGES REQUESTED at the SAME sha, 19h40m ago
    #1974  head 0c09fe8e2c  CHANGES REQUESTED at the SAME sha, 5 min after the commit
    #1978  head 17e27888ce  CHANGES REQUESTED at the SAME sha, 4 min after the commit
    #2001  head ffac563445  CHANGES REQUESTED at the SAME sha
    #1984  head 2096f9c17e  NO VERDICT -- genuinely unreviewed, 18h old

Four of the five were refused within minutes of their head commit and have not moved since. Every one of those four would have been a second verdict on byte-identical code, and because aida review record is a blind full replace, each would have destroyed between one and four existing findings to restate them. So I reviewed #1984 and reported on the rest.

The queue is telling us the wrong thing. Five reviewer-routed entries reads as five reviews outstanding; the real number was one. If a routed reviewer entry does not carry whether a verdict already exists at the current head, it cannot distinguish work-to-do from work-already-done -- which is the same absent-versus-present confusion as the rest of today, applied to the queue itself.

#1984 / TASK-1279: CHANGES REQUESTED recorded, hold verified armed on both layers.

The code is good and I want to say so first: a non-Claude resolved vendor routes to cold_boot_and_run with AgentSeat::Advisor, so per-seat model and effort still apply, and the dry-run path reports the same branch. Acceptance 3 is met -- codex_hooks_match_settings at aida-core/src/scaffolding/codex_hooks.rs:131 is a real test comparing both embedded hook sets. The matrix is a genuinely good document.

WHAT BLOCKS IT IS THE SHAPE WE HAVE NOW SEEN THREE TIMES TODAY, and this instance is the starkest because the artifact argues against itself. docs/agents/seat-parity.md ends with: "Do not claim completion until the first wave has merged at least one drain-mode spec behind the Codex advisor gate." The spec's status is already Done. The 06:23Z audit reports advisor-seat events 0 and product-seat events 0. Commit 2096f9c17e carries the (TASK-1279) trailer, so this merge auto-completes a spec whose central criterion the document itself says is not met -- and implementer/reviewer parity was already proven before this spec existed, so criterion 4 IS the spec.

AND ONE GAP IS SELF-BURYING. Acceptance 2 requires each Degraded cell to have a filed spec. Both Codex Degraded cells -- Product and Advisor fork-from-live -- cite TASK-1279, the spec this merge completes. A gap whose filed spec is the spec that just closed cannot be found again. The correct pattern is in the same table: every Antigravity Degraded cell cites TASK-1207, separate and open. So the author knew the pattern and applied it to the other vendor.

Acceptance 1 is the softest of the four and I flagged it anyway: it requires every cell to have a proving command THAT WAS RUN with output pasted. Four probes are pasted against roughly twenty-four non-N/A cells, and two of the four are --help invocations. A --help proves the flag parses, not that the seat works. The matrix reads as evidence and is mostly a plan.

REMEDY IS YOURS AND IT IS NOT CODE: split the dogfood waves to a successor spec and scope criterion 4 out explicitly, the same treatment you gave BUG-1454 criterion 7, and repoint the two Codex Degraded cells at that successor. Then it approves.

ON #1972, separately: my previous mail covers it. Short version -- reviewing it cannot unblock #2009, the blocker is an operator design decision that the spec title has been stating for nineteen hours, and the fail-open decide() is the third instance of the wildcard-swallows-the-unknown-case class.

Both verdicts recorded tonight carry no reviewed_sha in their PR-keyed handshake, for the stale-binary reason in TASK-1-163. The spec-keyed files have full provenance.
subject: Triage: 4 of 5 queued reviews were already refused at their current head; #1984 reviewed - CHANGES REQUESTED, and the document argues against its own spec status
